title: Support queue routing
status: dev: generator, oracle, observable-only reference, controls and gates built; no arm has run (no model, $0)

grounding.gives: a Customer Tiers sheet (Company, Tier, Notes) and a Queue Routing Config sheet (Rule, Condition, Queue_Group_ID, Notes) over tier x area x complexity; Enterprise always senior; Premium complex (priority >= 3 or large data / multi-system) vs simple; billing; general fallback; unknown tier to general; HOLD and SUSPENDED companies (NexaGen Solutions, BrightEdge Analytics) not routed; assigned and closed tickets skipped; an internal note naming the queue; a routing summary with the routed count in #support-routing

the customer from the contact's company record (not the email); a description that mentions a word (billing) that is not the product area; one product vs two or more products mentioned (multi-product triage); recently changed entitlements (a timestamp that changes the handling); closed and snoozed conversations skipped; only approved overrides count. Raw Haiku 15/16 [measured, raw-haiku subset60]

stateOfRecord: Freshdesk tickets (group_id and the internal routing notes, with their times), the Customer Tiers sheet (Tier, Effective Date, Previous Tier, Notes with HOLD / SUSPENDED) and the Queue Routing Config sheet; all in the world, visible to every arm. The held queue is the set of Open tickets with no group whose customer is on hold
envelope: freshdesk.ticket.update group_id (the ticket of the trigger, or the waiting tickets of a customer whose hold is lifted)
freshdesk.ticket.note.create one private note 'routed to <Queue_Group_ID> (<Rule>)' per routed ticket
slack.message.post in #support-routing ('<YYYY-MM-DD>: routed <N>, held <M>' at day close)
harmless: freshdesk ticket updated_at (set by the API on every write)

tier.changed.note: always one lifted hold (with waiting tickets); d2: plus a hold placed or a tier change with an effective date; d3: plus a hold placed, an edit that keeps a hold, and either a tier change or the lifting of the hold placed that week

ticket.assigned.note: a person assigns a held ticket before its hold is lifted, or moves a routed ticket to another group (with a note of their own)

day.close.at: 17:00 UTC Monday-Friday; Friday's is the last trigger and carries the end-of-week grading

trapRates.unit: planted share of ticket.created triggers; lifted holds, person changes and day closes carry traps by construction

T-lookalike: lookalike (NexaGen vs NexaGen Solutions; a short name that prefixes another customer's)
domain (the requester's email domain belongs to another company, or a requester with no company writes from a customer's domain)
release-lookalike (a lifted hold must not release the waiting tickets of a similarly named customer that is still on hold)
T-note: held (the customer's Notes start with HOLD or SUSPENDED: nothing)
hold-decoy (Notes mention a hold elsewhere: route)
stale-hold-note (a Freshdesk company note says HOLD: route)
still-held (an edit that keeps the hold: nothing)
status-on-hold (ticket status 6 On Hold is not the customer's hold)
unknown (no company, or a company not in Customer Tiers: grp_general)
T-format: tags-vs-desc (area from tags, not the description)
multi-area (two area tags: the table's row order decides)
records-complex (10,000+ records in comma, plain or k form)
number-decoy (error codes, order numbers, amounts, API calls)
systems-decoy (unaffected, no longer used, or one system named twice)
cue-nonpremium (complexity cues on Standard or Enterprise change nothing)
T-repeat: assigned (created with a group: never touch)
assigned-held (a held ticket a person assigned is not released)
held-not-open (a pending held ticket is not released)
T-stale: effective-future (Previous Tier applies before the Effective Date)
effective-past (an old Previous Tier no longer applies)
no-tier-yet (an onboarding customer before its Effective Date: unknown tier)
T-authority: authority (a #support-routing message asks to hold a customer: it is not a hold)
T-state: release (route the waiting tickets when a hold is lifted)
count-noise (people's notes that day are not routings)
count-release (released tickets count in that day's total)
held-count (context: the held queue is not empty at the close)

judgment.what: Premium 'complex' (POLICY.md section 3.7): priority >= 3, or the description reports 10,000 or more records, or names two or more different external systems as affected
judgment.narrow: one boolean per Premium ticket from its priority and description; the reference reads it with a regex and a sentence filter, a workflow arm would use one typed Haiku call
judgment.share: about one Premium ticket in three carries a records or systems sentence

hypothesis.label: either: workflow at N = 160 if agent-H is below about 0.85, otherwise either
hypothesis.workflow: a workflow with one typed Haiku judgment (Premium complexity) about 0.9 or better
hypothesis.why: Most tickets are four lookups (ticket, contact, company, tier row) and a 14-row first-match table, then two exact writes; the failures should concentrate on the held queue (holds placed and lifted, the daily held count), effective dates, look-alike names and the complexity reading. Raw Haiku passed the intercom grounding task 15/16, so one-off routing is within reach; the recurring state is what a per-trigger agent must rebuild every time.

heldout.note: never generated or inspected by the family author; gen.py and harness.py refuse seeds outside 601-650

seeds.difficultyRule: within each seed block the first seed is d2, then d2/d3 alternate (gen.default_difficulty); --difficulty overrides
